'''Jean-Loup Waldspurger''' (born 2 July 1953) is a French [[mathematician]] working on the [[Langlands program]] and related areas. He proved [[Waldspurger's theorem]], the [[Waldspurger formula]], and the local [[Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture]] for orthogonal groups. He played a role in the proof of the [[Fundamental lemma (Langlands program)|fundamental lemma]], reducing the conjecture to a version for [[Lie algebras]]. This formulation was ultimately proven by [[Ngô Bảo Châu]].

==Education==
Waldspurger attained his [[doctorate]] at [[École normale supérieure]] in 1980, under supervision of [[Marie-France Vignéras]].

== Scientific work ==
J.-L. Waldspurger's work concerns the theory of automorphic forms. He highlighted the links between Fourier coefficients of modular shapes of half full weight and function values L or periods of modular shapes of full weight. With C. Moeglin, he demonstrated Jacquet's conjecture describing the discrete spectrum of the GL(n) groups.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Mœglin | first1=C. | last2=Waldspurger | first2=J.-L. | title=Le spectre résiduel de <math>{\rm GL}(n)</math> | journal=Annales scientifiques de l'École normale supérieure | publisher=Societe Mathematique de France | volume=22 | issue=4 | year=1989 | issn=0012-9593 | doi=10.24033/asens.1595 | pages=605–674| doi-access=free }}</ref> Other works are devoted to orbital integrals on p-adic groups: unipotent orbital integrals, proof of the conjecture of Langlands-Shelstad transfer conditional on the "fundamental lemma" (which was later proved by Ngo-Bao-Chau<ref name="Ngô 2010 pp. 1–169">{{cite journal | last=Ngô | first=Bao Châu | title=Le lemme fondamental pour les algèbres de Lie | journal=Publications mathématiques de l'IHÉS | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=111 | issue=1 | date=23 April 2010 | issn=0073-8301 | doi=10.1007/s10240-010-0026-7 | pages=1–169 | s2cid=118103635 | url=http://www.numdam.org/articles/10.1007/s10240-010-0026-7/ | language=fr| arxiv=0801.0446 }}</ref>). J.-L. Waldspurger proved the Gross-Prasad conjecture for SO(N) groups on a p-adic field. With C. Moeglin, he wrote two large volumes establishing the stable trace formula for twisted spaces.<ref name="Moeglin Waldspurger 2016 p. ">{{cite book | last1=Moeglin | first1=Colette | last2=Waldspurger | first2=Jean-Loup | title=Stabilisation de la formule des traces tordue. Volume 1 | publication-place=Cham | date=2016 | isbn=978-3-319-30049-8 | oclc=965778158 | language=fr | page=}}</ref>

Some recent publications are available on its website.<ref>{{cite web|title=Publications|url=https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~jean-loup.waldspurger/|date=|access-date=2019-09-05|archive-date=2020-08-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809113440/https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~jean-loup.waldspurger/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Awards==
He won the {{ill|Mergier–Bourdeix Prize|fr|Prix Mergier-Bourdeix}} of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 1996. He was awarded the 2009 [[Clay Research Award]] for his results in [[p-adic analysis|''p''-adic harmonic analysis]]. He was elected as a member of [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/membre/election_051217.pdf|title=DIX-HUIT NOUVEAUX MEMBRES ÉLUS A L'ACADÉMIE DES SCIENCES|date=6 December 2017|access-date=10 December 2017|archive-date=20 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211120213511/https://www.academie-sciences.fr/pdf/membre/election_051217.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>
